trust_decision.summary: A bind zone line is built by plain string concatenation of record + tab + ttl + tab + class + tab + type + [prio] + content, so any field that can carry whitespace, a quote or ';' forges additional resource records in the generated zone file; at the pinned commit only 'content' is character-filtered, while the record label is merely lower-cased, punycode-checked and length-limited and the RR type is used only for a case-sensitive per-type validation dispatch, so both record and type reach the serializer verbatim. The decision is made in DomainZones::add and the injection lands in DnsEntry::__toString.

landing_point.why: The advisory names DomainZones.add and this is the one line where the record string is normalised; the type parameter read at lib/Froxlor/Api/Commands/DomainZones.php:93 is right above the same validation block, so both fields of the report point at this method.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue that the zone-line writer only re-emits rows that DomainZones.add has already validated, so once the handler rejects bad record/type values the serializer and the separate PowerDNS export look like downstream plumbing - the stored rows from before the upgrade and the pdns INSERT at lib/Froxlor/Cron/Dns/PowerDNS.php:155-176 are then left writing record/type raw.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Records that are legitimately not hostnames must keep working: the apex/wildcard markers '@' and '*' (special-cased in the handler), underscore labels such as '_dmarc', 'dkim<id>._domainkey' and SRV '_service._proto' labels that froxlor generates itself, and the NAPTR type which already has its own validator but was absent from the UI type list. A fix that uses validateDomain() without the underscore flag, a plain [a-z0-9-] label regex, or a whitelist copied from the old dropdown silently rejects records froxlor itself emits; the published fix had to call validateDomain(..., true) on a '.froxlor.test' suffixed label and add NAPTR to the form.

O6_input_shapes: record carrying control characters / NUL / CR / LF / DEL / non-ASCII (stripped to printable ASCII before anything else)
record given as a bare label ('www2'), as an underscore label ('_dmarc', 'dkim1._domainkey'), as a wildcard ('*.sub'), or as the special values '@' and '*'
record in upper case or mixed case (lower-cased before the label check)
record containing '--' (punycode error) or longer than 63 characters (separate branches that skip the new label check)
type with surrounding whitespace, or in lower/mixed case ('mx', 'txt') - now uppercased so the per-type validation dispatch is actually hit
type outside the 14 supported RR types (A, AAAA, CAA, CNAME, DNAME, LOC, MX, NAPTR, NS, RP, SRV, SSHFP, TLSA, TXT) - now rejected
record reaching the non-ASCII path: punycode conversion happens before the label check, so the check sees the encoded form

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Record label taken from a subdomain row: Dns::createDomainZone copies str_replace('.' . domain, '', subdomain.domain) straight into a required A/AAAA/TXT entry, so a subdomain name becomes a zone record label without the new label rule; SubDomains::add keeps anything its default Validate::validate pattern allows (spaces, ';', '"', '(' - only \r\n\t\f\0 are refused) when system.validate_domain is off.
O8_uncovered_routes.where: lib/Froxlor/Dns/Dns.php:154-188 (label built at :155, emitted at :159-168); source at lib/Froxlor/Api/Commands/SubDomains.php:147-155; lib/Froxlor/Validate/Validate.php:84-95
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the subdomain feature, not the DNS editor, and SubDomains::add already calls Validate::validate and (optionally) validateDomain, so a solver reads the label as validated elsewhere and out of this advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (Froxlor\Dns and Froxlor\Api\Commands\SubDomains) two hops from the landing point, reached only through the cron/bind generation path

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bulk/multi-record add or a zone-import action in the same command that reuses the INSERT block
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler inserts one record per submit; a maintainer adding 'add several records at once' or 'import a zone' would naturally copy this INSERT block and the existing per-type checks while omitting the two new record/type guards.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the PowerDNS backend writing name/type/content into the pdns records table raw
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already a second transport for exactly the same three fields (lib/Froxlor/Cron/Dns/PowerDNS.php:161-173) with no validation, so a second writer added next to it would look equally like plumbing.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: escaping/validation at the zone-line serializer itself (quote or reject whitespace in record and type before concatenation)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The serializer is where the injection actually happens and is fed by every producer, so a maintainer hardening the sink instead of the handlers is a one-file, natural change - and a hidden test can seed domain_dns_entries directly and call DomainZones.get / Dns::createDomainZone (DomainZones.php:417-418).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second panel form (customer-side or admin-side) passing dns_type straight to the API while relying on the select list in lib/formfields/formfield.dns_add.php:39-58
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The frontend already forwards Request::post('dns_type') unvalidated and the dropdown is only a UI hint, so any new editor form would look protected by its dropdown.
